origin.description:
dir_ls() is equivalent to the ls command. It returns filenames as a
named fs_path character vector. The names are equivalent to the values,
which is useful for passing onto functions like purrr::map_dfr().

dir_info() is equivalent to ls -l and a shortcut for
file_info(dir_ls()).

dir_map() applies a function fun() to each entry in the path and returns
the result in a list.

dir_walk() calls fun for its side-effect and returns the input path.
origin.usage:
dir_ls(
  path = ".",
  all = FALSE,
  recurse = FALSE,
  type = "any",
  glob = NULL,
  regexp = NULL,
  invert = FALSE,
  fail = TRUE,
  ...,
  recursive
)

dir_map(
  path = ".",
  fun,
  all = FALSE,
  recurse = FALSE,
  type = "any",
  fail = TRUE
)

dir_walk(
  path = ".",
  fun,
  all = FALSE,
  recurse = FALSE,
  type = "any",
  fail = TRUE
)

dir_info(
  path = ".",
  all = FALSE,
  recurse = FALSE,
  type = "any",
  regexp = NULL,
  glob = NULL,
  fail = TRUE,
  ...
)

arguments.name: path
arguments.text: A character vector of one or more paths.

arguments.name: all
arguments.text: If TRUE hidden files are also returned.

arguments.name: recurse
arguments.text:
If TRUE recurse fully, if a positive number the number of levels
to recurse.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text:
File type(s) to return, one or more of "any", "file", "directory",
"symlink", "FIFO", "socket", "character_device" or "block_device".

arguments.name: glob
arguments.text: A wildcard aka globbing pattern (e.g. *.csv) passed on to grep() to filter paths.

arguments.name: regexp
arguments.text: A regular expression (e.g. [.]csv$) passed on to grep() to filter paths.

arguments.name: invert
arguments.text: If TRUE return files which do not match

arguments.name: fail
arguments.text:
Should the call fail (the default) or warn if a file cannot be
accessed.
Additional arguments passed to grep.

arguments.name: recursive
arguments.text: (Deprecated) If TRUE recurse fully.

arguments.name: fun
arguments.text: A function, taking one parameter, the current path entry.

dir_walk() calls fun for its side-effect and returns the input path.
origin.example:
.old_wd <- setwd(tempdir())
dir_ls(R.home("share"), type = "directory")

# Create a shorter link
link_create(system.file(package = "base"), "base")

dir_ls("base", recurse = TRUE, glob = "*.R")

# If you need the full paths input an absolute path
dir_ls(path_abs("base"))

dir_map("base", identity)

dir_walk("base", str)

dir_info("base")

# Cleanup
link_delete("base")
setwd(.old_wd)

translation.details:
dir_ls() is equivalent to the ls command. It returns filenames as a
named fs_path character vector. The names are equivalent to the values,
which is useful for passing onto functions like purrr::map_dfr().

dir_info() is equivalent to ls -l and a shortcut for
file_info(dir_ls()).

dir_map() applies a function fun() to each entry in the path and returns
the result in a list.

dir_walk() calls fun for its side-effect and returns the input path.
translation.example:
share = subprocess.check_output(["Rscript", "-e", "cat(R.home('share'))"], text=True).strip()
show(dir_ls(share, type="directory"))
link_create(path_package("base")[0], "base")
show(dir_ls("base", recurse=True, glob="*.R"))
show(dir_ls(path_abs("base")))
show(dir_map("base", lambda name: name))
dir_walk("base", lambda name: print(name))
show(dir_info("base"))
link_delete("base")
